ops.title: Dead-holder-with-orphans recovery design (2026-07 incident)
ops.body:
The 2026-07 incident class and the recovery design spread across internal/daemon/server.go, internal/daemon/holderstate.go, and internal/cli/doctor.go.

## The incident signature
A crashed mount holder leaves its go-nfsv4 servers orphaned: the kernel mounts stay in the mount table, and the orphaned servers answer EPERM through EVERY mount (which is why a probe EPERM/EACCES reads as ErrProbeWedged, never ErrProbeMissing — the 2026-07 misread). No successor holder can reap them: the holder's own reaper is direct-children-only.

## Recovery design
- Detection: holderState latches servedMounts while healthy-with-mounts (surviving the degraded Health-ok/List-failed step a crash often tears down through). markUnhealthy fires onLostWithMounts exactly once per death, off the lock — the healthy→unreachable transition of a holder that was serving mounts.
- The Server wires onLostWithMounts to sweepHolderOrphans (async, wg-tracked) so recovery short-circuits the per-row remount breaker's five-strike wait.
- sweepHolderOrphans: (1) reapPoolOrphans kills any-generation go-nfsv4 orphans bound under the pool's mount roots — the mux go-nfsv4 (bound to the mux root) and legacy per-dir servers (under accounts/). Carcass-gated AND kill-time-reconfirmed in fusekit, so a live holder's healthy servers are never candidates; unconditional because a dead holder cannot own a live mount. (2) Then the idle-gated sweep force-unmounts the shared mux root when no live session rides it.
- Cold-start hole: a daemon starting over an already-dead holder sees no healthy→unreachable transition, so the loss hook can never cover it — reconcileOverlays runs reapPoolOrphans FIRST, unconditionally, on every startup (safe because carcass-gated).
- Live sessions defer the force-unmount but NEVER the reap: force-unmounting a busy NFS mirror panics the kernel (kernel-panic class), so a bound session pushes the unmount to a later sweep and the operator must relaunch those sessions.
- doctor (reportOrphanedHolder) surfaces the signature — holder unreachable + mounts still in the kernel table — and names the blocking session PIDs the operator must relaunch.
ops.when: working on holder-death recovery, orphaned go-nfsv4 reaping (sweepHolderOrphans/reapPoolOrphans/sweepOrphanMuxRoot), onLostWithMounts, doctor's 'mount holder orphans' line, or diagnosing EPERM through fuse mounts
